title: Willow Fintech compliance & encryption scoping
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Redwood hosting options. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with emphasis on KMS/BYOK, audit logs, retention, SSO/SAML and SOC2/ISO evidence. SE provided high-level architecture notes and tradeoffs; discussed next steps for security docs, SOC2 artifact pack, pilot scope and an on-prem connectivity checklist.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-02 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Recording started
Attendees: Lydia Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Amir (Willow), Sofia (Willow), Ben (Willow), Tanya (Willow)

[00:00:00] Lydia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I will kick us off — I'm Lydia, AE on the account, and Ravi is our solutions engineer. Quick audio check?
[00:00:07] Amir: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Lydia.
[00:00:10] Ravi: Great. Our goal today is to understand Willow's compliance checklist and surface any blockers for Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment. We'll try to map requirements to capabilities.
[00:00:19] Sofia: To frame it — Willow is a regulated payments platform, so SOC2 is a hard requirement, ISO may be optional but desirable, and we have strict controls on keys and logs. We also have a timeline — we need a pilot within eight weeks.
[00:00:30] Lydia: Perfect, can you run through stakeholders? Who signs off, and who will run the pilot?
[00:00:35] Ben: Platform will own the POC, I'll be hands-on. Security (Sofia) will validate controls, and Legal (Tanya) will look at contracts and DPA. CFO will look at cost after initial run.
[00:00:44] Ravi: Understood. Quick Q: do you have existing KMS provider preferences? AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or do you need HSM-on-prem?
[00:00:52] Amir: We're primarily AWS but we have an on-prem HSM for some payment keys. For POC, we'd prefer BYOK into AWS KMS, but we may need HSM-level evidence for production.
[00:01:02] Sofia: Also need to know about key rotation/exports — we can't have Redwood holding plaintext key material for customer-sensitive artifacts.
[00:01:09] Ravi: Yeah, we support several models. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integration (BYOK) — Redwood never sees raw key material; we use envelope encryption and the platform stores only wrapped keys. For Private, you can bring an HSM via PKCS#11 in the VPC or integrate with your HSM for an on‑prem deployment.
[00:01:28] Sofia: When you say "we never see" — can you show an architecture diagram later for the audit folks? It's critical for SOC2 evidence.
[00:01:35] Lydia: Absolutely. We'll share a security pack that includes architecture artifacts, SOC2 summary, pen test reports and our data flow diagrams.
[00:01:41] [00:01:41] Ben: On logs — what's the retention? We need 365 days of immutable audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[00:01:47] Ravi: We ship audit trails and request logs; retention is configurable. Hosted customers can either push logs to their S3 or we can forward to SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. Immutable retention for 12 months is supported for both Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have options but need to scope legal SLAs for immutability.
[00:02:03] Sofia: Do you support WORM (write once read many) or object lock? We rely on S3 Object Lock for immutability.
[00:02:09] Ravi: We can forward to your S3 with object lock enabled on your side; Redwood's hosted log retention uses our managed storage but for legal immutability we recommend forwarding to customer-controlled buckets with Object Lock — that's typical.
[00:02:20] Lydia: Quick note — sometimes transcripts say K-V cash, that's our KV cache, so if that shows up in the SOC2 diagrams, it's the in-memory cache for model state.
[00:02:29] Amir: ha, noted — transcriptions are fun.
[00:02:33] [00:02:33] Sofia: SSO is another big one. We use SAML with IdP (Okta) for staff access and need SCIM provisioning to keep groups in sync. Can Redwood integrate?
[00:02:43] Ravi: Yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning users/groups. For Dedicated and Private you can also federate to your IdP over an internal connection. We also support RBAC with role mapping — you can map Okta groups -> Redwood roles and then restrict actions like model rollout, billing, and audit access.
[00:03:02] Ben: For RBAC — can we separate developers vs production ops? We need least-privilege by environment and also per-customer tenant isolation since we run multiple product lines.
[00:03:10] Ravi: We support multi-tenant workspaces with per-workspace RBAC. In Dedicated, you get stronger isolation at the infra level — separate GPU pools, VPC segmentation. Private gives you full network isolation into your VPC. Hosted is logically multi-tenant with RBAC enforced at the platform layer.
[00:03:27] [00:03:27] Sofia: Do you have MFA enforcement and device posture checks for SSO?
[00:03:31] Lydia: We support enforcing SSO MFA via the IdP; device posture can be handled through conditional access in Okta — Redwood honors the SAML attributes.
[00:03:39] Amir: Can you provide SAML metadata and a test flow for our IdP team?
[00:03:42] Ravi: We'll send SAML metadata and a short SCIM test harness. I'll include steps to map groups and sample assertions.
[00:03:48] [00:03:48] Tanya: On the legal side — we need to confirm data residency and deletion. If a model stores derived embeddings or intermediate artifacts, what's the retention and how do we verify deletion?
[00:03:58] Ravi: Good question. By default, Redwood does not persist raw customer inputs beyond request tracing windows unless you enable caching or long-term embeddings. There are tunables: ephemeral mode where no data is stored beyond the request, or persistent embeddings bucket which you control. For deletion we provide an API to purge customer artifacts and an audit event showing purge completion. For Hosted customers who want provable deletion we recommend pinning storage to customer-owned buckets or Private deployment.
[00:04:23] Sofia: We need documented deletion SLA (e.g., delete within 24 hours and provide audit). Is that in your SOC2 pack?
[00:04:29] Lydia: We'll include deletion SLAs and API semantics in the DPA addendum. For stricter guarantees Dedicated/Private offers more control and easier attestation.
[00:04:36] [00:04:36] Amir: What about telemetry — do you keep message content in traces? We can't have content in centralized logs.
[00:04:43] Ravi: Traces are tokenized and content is redacted by default; full content is only stored if you opt-in for debugging and then it's marked as sensitive and stored in a customer bucket with customer ownership.
[00:04:55] Ben: On the infrastructure side — if we pick Dedicated, how is the network connectivity set up? VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or private link?
[00:05:04] Ravi: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-like connectivity depending on cloud provider. For Private we provision within your VPC; we'll provide a connectivity checklist including security groups, egress rules, NAT, and routing.
[00:05:16] Sofia: Pen testing — do you allow customers to run pentests against the service endpoints?
[00:05:20] Lydia: Yes, we have a pentest policy and a scheduled window; we can coordinate and provide a scope doc. We'll also include our recent third-party pen test report in the security pack.
[00:05:28] [00:05:28] Amir: Encryption in transit — TLS versions and ciphers? We need TLS1.2 minimum, and for sensitive endpoints possibly TLS1.3 only.
[00:05:35] Ravi: TLS 1.2+ supported, TLS 1.3 available. Cipher suite lists are in the hardening guide we'll share. We also support mutual TLS for private endpoints if you want client certs.
[00:05:46] Sofia: Key rotation — can you rotate keys without downtime? We need rotation policies and support for automatic rewraps.
[00:05:52] Ravi: Yes, envelope encryption allows rewraps in the background; the runtime supports key versioning and seamless rotation. We have documented rotation playbooks and we'll share those.
[00:06:02] [00:06:02] Ben: Pricing angle — Dedicated is more predictable but higher commit; Hosted gives faster time-to-prove. We're trying to balance cost vs control. Any guidelines?
[00:06:11] Lydia: We can propose a pilot on Hosted with BYOK + logs to your S3 for immutability so you can start quickly, then move to Dedicated if you need infra separation. Private is recommended if you require full on‑prem HSM integration. We'll surface cost delta in the proposal.
[00:06:26] Sofia: A concern — if billing metadata leaks PII into logs, how do you handle tokenization?
[00:06:32] Ravi: We support field-level redaction and PII scrubbing before logs leave the runtime; we can configure scrubbing rules on a per-customer basis.
[00:06:40] Lydia: Quick process note — for SOC2/ISO validation you will typically ask for our control matrix and sample evidence. We will provide a mapping doc (controls -> artifacts) and package of artifacts including our latest SOC2 Type II report, vulnerability scan results, and operational runbooks.
[00:06:56] [00:06:56] Sofia: Great. We also want to run a small workload benchmark to ensure latency targets are met for low-latency features. Can we run that in POC?
[00:07:04] Ravi: Yes, we can enable a canary on Hosted or reserved nodes on Dedicated for benchmark traffic. We'll provide a benchmarking harness and a sample prompt set to run. For the POC we recommend measuring p50/p95 latency and token cost impact with caching enabled.
[00:07:21] Amir: One more on audit logs — are logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for legal support.
[00:07:27] Ravi: We produce signed log entries and can configure log shipping with integrity checks. If you push to your S3 with object lock and checksums, you get strong chain-of-custody.
[00:07:36] [00:07:36] Ben: Who signs off on SLAs and what are typical SLAs for Dedicated?
[00:07:40] Lydia: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; commercial will include the SLA in the contract. Hosted has best-effort availability but we offer enterprise SLAs as an add-on. We'll loop in sales/contract to detail that.
[00:07:52] Sofia: Can you also confirm data residency — can we pin a region? We must ensure EU data stays in EU.
[00:07:58] Ravi: You can pin region for Dedicated and Private. Hosted allows region preference but not strict region pinning unless under an enterprise arrangement. We'll call that out.
[00:08:08] [00:08:08] Lydia: Okay, practical next steps — we'll send the SOC2 pack, SAML metadata, SCIM test harness, and a POC plan. Anything else?
[00:08:17] Sofia: Please include your KMS integration docs and HSM options, and a sample deletion confirmation payload.
[00:08:23] Lydia: We'll include that.
[00:08:25] Amir: Also share a connectivity checklist for Dedicated and Private so Ben can pre-scope networking.
[00:08:29] Lydia: Will do.
[00:08:31] [00:08:31] Ravi: Action item — I'll prepare a short architecture diagram showing BYOK flow, envelope encryption, and log pipeline.
[00:08:38] Ben: Good.
[00:08:40] Tanya: Legal will need the DPA template and data processing terms.
[00:08:43] Lydia: I'll have contracts team send the DPA and a draft SOW for the POC.
[00:08:48] [00:08:48] Sofia: One process question — for evidence we may request sysadmins to inspect network configs for Dedicated; do you accommodate on-site audits or remote evidence only?
[00:08:58] Ravi: We support both — most customers prefer remote evidence (logs, screenshots, configs, jumpbox sessions). For Private you can do hands-on audits since it's in your VPC. For Hosted, remote only.
[00:09:10] Amir: timeline revisit — eight weeks to pilot start, then three months for production decision. Any blockers?
[00:09:16] Lydia: That seems doable. We'll aim to deliver docs within 3 business days and schedule a technical walkthrough with Ravi and Ben for the POC kickoff.
[00:09:25] [00:09:25] Transcript noise/interruptions: (overlap)
[00:09:27] Lydia: Alright — recap and next steps in the chat. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels — Speaker 5 is the calendar placeholder for a late attendee, and some infra terms (KV cache) may be transcribed as K-V cash or similar.
